author: Karl Rock
description:
Deep in rural Sindh, Pakistan, stands the massive Kot Diji Fort. It is a stunning, lesser known piece of architecture that towers over the surrounding date palm plantations and farmland. Yet, as you explore the walls of this ancient royal guest room, the beauty is marred by careless graffiti scratched into the stone.

It is a sobering reminder that protecting these sites is not just about government preservation. It requires respect from everyone who visits.

Beyond the vandalism, the fort offers a fascinating glimpse into the past. Walking through the royal guest house, you can still spot intricate details like stone fireplaces designed to keep residents warm during harsh winters. It is a place that deserves to be admired, not altered.
title: Why do people deface their own history?

author: Karl Rock
description:
These singers from Kot Diji have found their own slice of fame online, sharing their culture with the world.

Here, they perform a Manqabat, a form of Islamic devotional poetry and song that praises and honours revered religious figures. Their powerful chants, alongside joyful greetings for the New Year and Eid, reflect the deep cultural and religious traditions of Sindh.

Performed against the ancient stone walls of Kot Diji, their voices connect the history of this place with the people who live here today. It’s a powerful reminder that history is never truly in the past. It lives on through the traditions, music and voices of the people who inherit it.
title: Kot Diji’s Famous Singers
